hints: Notice the notation $^{A}_{Z}X$: the upper number is nucleon number $A$ and the lower number is proton number $Z$ for E, G, M and Q.
Recall that an uncharged atom has orbital electrons equal to $Z$, isotopes share $Z$, alpha decay changes $A$ by -4 and $Z$ by -2, and beta-minus changes $Z$ by +1 with $A$ unchanged.
Track E $^{28}_{14}$ through +1 neutron then -1 alpha-particle, and track M $^{25}_{12}$ through beta-minus, then compare $A$ and $Z$ with M and Q.
walkthrough: Identify $A$ (top) and $Z$ (bottom): E is $A=28$, $Z=14$; G is $A=25$, $Z=15$; M is $A=25$, $Z=12$; Q is $A=24$, $Z=13$.

Recall the rules: neutron absorption adds $+1$ to $A$ only, alpha-particle $^{4}_{2}He$ emission subtracts $4$ from $A$ and $2$ from $Z$, and beta-minus emission leaves $A$ unchanged and adds $+1$ to $Z$.
Test option C: E absorbs a neutron: $A = 28+1 = 29$, $Z = 14$. Then emits alpha: $A = 29-4 = 25$, $Z = 14-2 = 12$. This is $^{25}_{12}$, which is M.
Check the others: Q has $Z=13$ so a neutral atom has 13 electrons, G and M have different $Z$ so are not isotopes, and M by beta-minus becomes $^{25}_{13}$, not $^{24}_{13}$Q.
The only fully matching transformation is E to M by neutron capture plus alpha emission. This is option C.

options.A: Q is $^{24}_{13}Q$, so proton number $Z=13$. An uncharged atom has electrons equal to $Z$, so 13 electrons, not 24.
options.B: Isotopes need the same $Z$ with different $A$. G has $Z=15$ and M has $Z=12$, so they are different elements.
options.C: Adding a neutron gives $A=29$, $Z=14$, then alpha emission subtracts $A=4$, $Z=2$ to give $A=25$, $Z=12$, which is M.
options.D: Beta-minus keeps $A=25$ and raises $Z$ from 12 to 13, giving $^{25}_{13}$, whereas Q is $^{24}_{13}$ with different nucleon number.
